text:
**Short answer:** for most campers, a 250-500Wh unit is the best fit. Bigger stations only make sense if you're running a fridge, cooler, or other heavy loads.

**Compact (weekend tent or car camping)**
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (~$249): 288Wh, 8.3 lb, LiFePO4. It's the top pick in PowerStationGearLab's guide. Jackery's own site has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, so buy the Plus from Amazon or other retailers. [Guide](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (~$269-299): 286Wh with a 600W inverter, expandable to 572Wh. [Guide](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (~$199): 288Wh, built-in lantern, 5-year warranty. Make sure you get the standard model with AC outlets, not the "C300 DC" variant. [Guide](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Bluetti EB3A** (~$179): the budget pick, 268Wh with a 600W inverter. [Guide](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)

**Larger (multi-day trips, electric cooler, van or overland)**
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2**: OutdoorGearLab's top pick for off-grid camping (tied for the highest test score, 81). It has 2,042Wh, weighs 39 lb, and can be found under $900 on sale (list $1,499). [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (~$799): TechRadar's pick for camping, with 1,070Wh. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2**: OutdoorGearLab's best value, on sale for under $530. It has a noisy fan and limited capacity. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Bluetti AC180** ($499): 1,152Wh LiFePO4 with an 1,800W inverter and a 5-year warranty. Code AFF5OFF took $24.95 off in the retailer's cart test, bringing it to about $474. It has no expansion port, and the $499 is for the station alone. [Buy at Bluetti via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180) (affiliate link, no extra cost to you). [Details](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180)

**Caveat:** the reviewers disagree on the small units. OutdoorGearLab's lab tests scored the Jackery Explorer 300 and Anker C300 fairly low (52 and 50 out of 100) and favored larger stations. PowerStationGearLab, which earns affiliate commissions, ranks the small ones highest. The small ones are still the lightest and cheapest to pack, but they won't run a fridge.

**How to choose:** a phone charge is about 10Wh, a CPAP is 30-60Wh per night (turn off the humidifier), and a lantern is about 5Wh per night. If that's all you need, a ~288Wh unit is plenty. If you want a cooler or fridge, go to 1,000Wh or more.

I couldn't pull direct Amazon product URLs from these results, so the links above go to the guides, except for the Bluetti link. Check current prices before buying, since sales are heating up ahead of Black Friday.

If you tell me what you'll be powering and for how many nights, I can narrow this to one pick.
